first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing creates the strongest pull toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly records that this lever bought acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention and carries an explicit do-not-generalize caveat. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is the one direction the inherited record affirmatively warns against, so I decline it despite the situational pressure. The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly one funnel problem rather than two: completion sits upstream of activation, so a completion shortfall would propagate into the activation number. That makes simplify_onboarding the higher-leverage single slot, with support from memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (field reduction at signup produced durable SMB activation lift). activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom and is my fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding record. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound but addresses a segment that is not the one under attack this quarter, and referral_incentive (memory_57) requires an established base that a weakening activation funnel is not currently replenishing. I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_91 because they are the two directions actually in contention and because both are the kind of claim that degrades on re-reading: I want to know whether memory_86's 'completion rate' lift was a real gain in accounts reaching value or merely a shorter funnel mechanically producing a higher completion percentage, and whether memory_91's 'first meaningful action' was a durable engagement gain or a one-week nudge. I do not need to verify memory_73 — its caveat is already recorded and it argues against an action I am not taking. Downstream value risk is live and flagged: cutting onboarding steps can strip out qualifying and configuration inputs that make later accounts convert and retain, so a completion lift could mask a decline in account quality. I will therefore instrument this on qualified-revenue and retention outcomes rather than completion rate alone, and hold it at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout — the inherited memories are consolidated summaries of prior conditions, not evidence about the current competitive environment, and the day-76 declines are themselves a signal that prior findings may have decayed.
